title: Cash divide widens between industry, retail funds
full_text:
Industry superannuation funds have reduced their cash holdings while retail funds have increased theirs, widening the allocation gap as industry funds lift their equity exposure.
Padua Wealth Data’s analysis of APRA investment allocation data across the March quarters of 2024, 2025 and 2026 found industry funds cut their cash weighting from 8.6 per cent to 6.3 per cent. Retail funds increased their allocation from 9.0 per cent to 9.4 per cent over the same period.
Fixed income allocations also moved in opposite directions, with industry funds reducing their weighting from 19.5 per cent to 18.3 per cent, while retail funds increased theirs from 18.9 per cent to 19.4 per cent.
The changes left retail funds holding larger allocations to both cash and fixed income by March 2026, although their overall equity weighting remained slightly higher than that of industry funds.
Industry funds’ core equity allocation climbed 3.7 percentage points, from 55.3 per cent to 59.0 per cent, narrowing the gap with retail funds, whose weighting rose by 0.6 percentage points to 60.3 per cent.
Almost all of the increase among industry funds came through unhedged international listed equities, which rose by 4.2 percentage points to 25.8 per cent of assets, suggesting the shift reflects a greater willingness to carry currency exposure.
Despite those changes, the analysis found the structural differences between the two sectors remained firmly in place, particularly in their exposure to listed and unlisted assets.
Infrastructure represented the largest allocation difference, accounting for around 10.9 per cent of industry fund assets at March 2026, compared with 4.2 per cent among retail funds.
Industry funds’ infrastructure exposure was predominantly unlisted, with these holdings representing around 9.7 per cent of total assets, against 1.7 per cent among retail funds.
Property allocations showed a similar divide, with industry funds holding around 5.0 per cent of assets in unlisted property, compared with 1.5 per cent among retail funds.
Retail funds held a larger allocation to listed property, at 3.9 per cent of assets, compared with 1.6 per cent among industry funds.
Both sectors reduced their overall property weightings across the three March quarters. Industry funds’ allocation declined from 7.4 per cent to 6.6 per cent, while retail funds’ allocation fell from 6.2 per cent to 5.5 per cent.
Source: Padua Wealth Data, APRA
Unlisted equity exposure also remained higher among industry funds, at around 5.1 per cent of assets. Retail funds held 1.9 per cent, down from 2.8 per cent in March 2024.
The analysis additionally showed industry funds directly managed around 66 per cent of their assets, compared with just under 12 per cent among retail funds, reinforcing the differences in how the two sectors manage their portfolios.
